How versions are numbered

A release gets a version of three numbers. The middle one goes up when there is something new to use or see: a tool, or a change to how the site looks or works. The last one goes up for fixes. The first stays at 0 while the site is still taking its shape.

The tool count is how many tools worked on the site that day. Releases before this page existed were numbered afterwards, from the history of the source, at the points where the site changed.

The version on every page's footer links here, so a saved copy of a tool still says which release it came from.

Files this page fetched from the network: 0. Save it with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) and it keeps working offline.

Translated by a machine, not checked by a native speaker. The English page is the reference.
